title: The Land Office transfer has no interface, no integration id and no operation, and the officer's registration has no published write surface
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E4-029, its Story paragraph, Acceptance criteria AC1 and AC2, and the Endpoints table); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.20.1 business objective, A2.20.2 integration points Land Office and AMIS, A2.20.2 step 3); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T5.1 external system interfaces, appendix T-A.1 endpoint inventory); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (feature row FEAT-AST-20, systems the Land Office and AMIS, kind User); _work/msr/context/S5.md (ownership rows of S5: six REST operations; connection matrix row S5 Asset)
section: APP s1 Story; s2 Business rationale; s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 1 to 3 and 12; s5 X9; s6 INVEST; s10 Authority; s12.1; s12.5; s12.8; s13; s19; CON s1 Story; s3; s7 C3 and C7; s12.1; s12.5; s12.8; s13; s19
description: Legacy AC2 says the transfer at the Land Office is recorded and the feature says in one sentence that the step stays a person and officer step, so the registration is an act outside the Workbench. No source then says how the record of that act reaches the service: the FSD A2.20.2 names the Land Office among the integration points but no interface exists for it, TSD S5 T5.1 lists SVAF, AMIS, RPS and HOME.SCB and no Land Office row, and no integration id covers it. The legacy Endpoints table gives this feature two operations and neither writes a registration, the ownership rows give S5 six operations of which four are other steps', and the officer's act on the case has no published task or write surface either. The two slices therefore declare the registration as a signal of AssetDisposalWorkflow and declare no Land Office interface, no file and no write operation, and the story cannot claim an external dependency row for it.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E4-029 Story line: tracks the Land Office transfer, which stays a person and officer step. Legacy Endpoints table rows: GET /api/recovery/v1/assets/{assetId} access R and POST /api/recovery/v1/assets/{assetId}/valuations access C, neither of which records a registration. FSD S5 A2.20.2 Integration points: Land Office, AMIS. TSD S5 T5.1 rows INT-11 SVAF, INT-12 AMIS, INT-13 RPS, INT-27 HOME.SCB, with no Land Office row. Epics 3 to 8 Specification FEAT-AST-20 systems column: Land Office, AMIS. Context pack ownership rows list GET /assets, GET /assets/{assetId}, GET /assets/{assetKey}, POST /assets/{assetId}/listings, POST /assets/{assetKey}/listings and POST /listings/{listingId}/rounds.
owner_role: Business lead of the Asset module with the solution architect of S5
proposed: Keep the Land Office as a person and officer step outside every service, carry the registration as the TITLE_REGISTERED signal of the case task, and declare no interface, no file, no operation and no X row for it.

title: No element of rwb_asset holds the title status, the Land Office registration date and reference or the custody release, and the ownership rows name only asset_sale and listing
source: _work/msr/context/S5.md (ownership rows of S5: tables asset_sale and listing); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T3.1 asset, listing and asset_sale field definitions DF-COL-028 to DF-COL-042 and DF-SAL-001 to DF-SAL-019, T3.2 LOV-HOLDING and LOV-LISTING); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.20.3.2 field catalog, A2.20.2 step 3 writes the decision log or interaction ledger entry); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E4-029, Data table naming document_custody)
section: APP s2 Business rationale; s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 4 and 8; s8 BR1 and BR7; s9 State transitions; s11 Data; s12.7; s13 Database; s19; CON s3; s11 Data; s12.7; s13 Open shapes
description: R-DIS-52 records the transfer and releases the documents, and neither fact has a home in the target data model of the service. The ownership rows of S5 give the service two tables, asset_sale and listing; TSD S5 T3.1 declares an asset object as EXTEND ACE Asset with DF-COL-028 to DF-COL-042 that carries asset type, transfer-in type, the transfer-in date, the book value and the holding status but no title status, no registration date and no registration reference; listing carries the sale channel, the prices, the round, the listed date and the status; asset_sale carries the contract and sale dates, the price, the fee, the taxes and the gain or loss of the sale. The legacy Data table names document_custody, whose fields belong to the document hub. A new column, a new list value or a new table for the title would be a data-model change no source authorises, so the registration reference rides in the decision record and the workflow signal and the statuses are the only writes.
evidence: TSD S5 T3.1 asset rows DF-COL-028 to DF-COL-042: id, case_id, collateral_id, asset_ref, asset_code, asset_type, transfer_in_type, from_segment, transfer_in_date, book_value, auction_purchase_price, repossessed_date, stock_date, holding_status, holding_cost_to_date. TSD S5 T3.1 listing rows DF-SAL-001 to DF-SAL-008 and asset_sale rows DF-SAL-009 to DF-SAL-019 carry no title or registration field. TSD S5 T3.2 LOV-HOLDING has HELD, LISTED, UNDER_OFFER, SOLD, TRANSFERRED, RENTED and LOV-LISTING has DRAFT, LIVE, UNDER_OFFER, SOLD, WITHDRAWN. Legacy Data table names document and document_custody with DF-DOC-001 to DF-DOC-011 and DF-DOC-018 to DF-DOC-024.
owner_role: Solution architect of S5 with the DB story owner of rwb_asset
proposed: Write listing status and asset holding status on the sold values of their lists, carry the registration date and reference in the decision record and the workflow input, and add no column, no list value and no table for the title.

title: The document custody release has no published operation on rwb-document and the plan carries no contract dependency for the boundary
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E4-029, Acceptance criteria AC2 and the Data table rows document and document_custody); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.20.3.1 rule R-DIS-52, A2.20.2 integration points); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (row R-DIS-52 systems column the Land Office and Document Hub); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (feature row FEAT-AST-20); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T5.2 cross-module interfaces names P5 for documents); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (both slices of RWB-E4-029: H, C, I and X lists, C empty)
section: APP s1 Story; s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow step 7; s5 X4; s8 BR4; s11 Data; s12.2; s12.8; s13; s19; CON s1 Story; s3; s7 C4; s11 Data; s12.2; s12.8; s19
description: R-DIS-52 releases the documents from custody and the legacy Data table names document and document_custody, which are the document hub's records. No source gives that release an operation: the FSD names the Document Hub only in the rule's systems column, TSD S5 T5.2 says calls go through the published interfaces with P5 for documents and publishes no name, and the ownership rows of S5 hold no document operation. The plan's contract dependency list of both slices is empty, although the release is a cross-service call in fact. The two slices therefore declare the release as a consumed row with a placeholder, on the document base, with one hop and a 2 s budget, and build it against a fake on Day 1.
evidence: Legacy AC2 Then line: release the documents from custody and record the transfer at the Land Office. Legacy Data table rows: document DF-DOC-001 to DF-DOC-011 and document_custody DF-DOC-018 to DF-DOC-024. Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-52 Systems: the Land Office, Document Hub. TSD S5 T5.2: calls go through the published Java interfaces, P3 for the case, P7 for the decision log, P4 for access and reference data, P5 for documents, P6 for notices, with no operation named. Plan C lists of RWB-S5-E4029-APP and RWB-S5-E4029-CON are empty.
owner_role: Owner of rwb-document (P5) with the tech lead of rwb-asset
proposed: Declare the custody release as a consumed row of rwb-document with an idempotency key, a 2 s budget and a fake, and treat it as a contract dependency in fact that the plan's empty C list does not carry.

title: Legacy AC3 of RWB-E4-029 owns R-DIS-02, the deed in lieu take-on that RWB-S5-E3020-APP already builds for the same rule
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E4-029, Acceptance criteria AC3; heading RWB-E3-020, Acceptance criteria AC2); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.2 the deed in lieu take-on of FEAT-AST-02 and A2.20 the Land Office transfer of FEAT-AST-20); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (row R-DIS-02); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (the acs lists of RWB-S5-E4029-APP and RWB-S5-E3020-APP)
section: APP s1 Story; s2 Business rationale; s7 note on AC3; s8 note; s19; CON s1 Story; s19
description: One rule is owned twice. Legacy RWB-E3-020 (FEAT-AST-02, take a property onto the books after a deed in lieu) carries R-DIS-02 as its AC2, and legacy RWB-E4-029 (FEAT-AST-20, the Land Office transfer) carries the same rule as its AC3; the FSD keeps the two features apart, A2.2 for the take-on and A2.20 for the transfer. The plan assigns AC3 to this slice, so the criterion is copied verbatim with its origin tag, but its behaviour - create the asset record from AMIS with the opening book value and answer ASSET_ON_BOOKS - is built once, in RWB-S5-E3020-APP, and this slice asserts it at the take-on boundary instead of implementing a second path to the same row.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E4-029 AC3: Given a case in state ASSET_PENDING_TAKE_ON, When dil transfer registered, Then create the asset record from AMIS with the opening book value, Then the case moves to ASSET_ON_BOOKS. Legacy RWB-E3-020 AC2 carries the same rule, event, action and target state. Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-02 from ASSET_PENDING_TAKE_ON on DIL_TRANSFER_REGISTERED to ASSET_ON_BOOKS. FSD S5 A2.2 is the deed in lieu take-on of FEAT-AST-02 and A2.20 is the Land Office transfer of FEAT-AST-20.
owner_role: Business analyst of the Asset module with the solution architect of S5
proposed: Keep AC3 verbatim with its origin tag, build R-DIS-02 only in RWB-S5-E3020-APP and assert it here as a regression at the take-on boundary, so that no second implementation of the rule exists.

title: R-DIS-53, the rejected transfer that blocks the title, sits in the state of this rule and is owned by no criterion and no story of the split
source: Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (rows R-DIS-52 and R-DIS-53); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.20.3.1 rule table and A2.20.4 exception flows); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E4-029, Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC4); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (the acs list of RWB-S5-E4029-APP)
section: APP s1 Story; s4 Flow step 11; s5 X9; s14 note; s19; CON s19
description: The state this story works ends in two ways and the split owns one of them. R-DIS-52 takes TITLE_TRANSFER_PENDING to ASSET_SOLD on a registered title; R-DIS-53 takes the same state to TITLE_BLOCKED when the Land Office or SCIS rejects the transfer, holds the transfer and raises a document task. The legacy story carries four criteria and none of them names R-DIS-53, the FSD lists it only in the rule table of another feature, and the plan gives no slice of any legacy key an AC that covers it. This slice therefore writes nothing for the rejection, names it as out of scope and records it here rather than inventing a criterion, a message or a task for it.
evidence: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-53: TITLE_TRANSFER_PENDING, event TRANSFER_REJECTED, condition SCIS or the Land Office rejects the transfer, action hold the transfer and raise a document task, to TITLE_BLOCKED, owner Sale officer, systems SCIS, the Land Office, Document Hub, timer 5 working days. Legacy RWB-E4-029 AC1 to AC4 cover R-DIS-52, R-DIS-02 and the not-recorded path only. No rule row of any other story of S5 names TRANSFER_REJECTED.
owner_role: Business analyst of the Asset module with the business lead
proposed: Leave the rejection out of this slice, name R-DIS-53 and its TITLE_BLOCKED state in the out-of-scope list of both stories, and open a story for it in the next realignment pass rather than inventing a criterion or a message now.

title: The plan carries no requirement id for either slice and TSD S5 T8 does not trace REQ-S5-008 or FEAT-AST-20
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E4-029, metadata table with no Requirement row); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (the reqs list of both slices, empty); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4 (requirement row REQ-S5-008); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (section Requirements served); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T8 requirement traceability)
section: APP s18 Traceability; the reqs key of both fragments; CON s18 Traceability
description: The traceability of the two stories needs one sourced requirement and the plan provides none. The legacy metadata table of RWB-E4-029 carries Epic, Module, Feature, Process, Priority, Depends on and Decision and no requirement row, and the plan's reqs list for both slices is empty. A requirement does exist at programme level: REQ-S5-008, title transfer is prepared and recorded for vehicles and for property, is a Must of E4 owned by the sale officer, and it covers FEAT-AST-19 and FEAT-AST-20 together. TSD S5 T8 traces only REQ-S5-001 to REQ-S5-010 against FEAT-AST-01 and FEAT-AST-08, with the story column reading written one epic ahead. Both slices therefore trace to REQ-S5-008 and FEAT-AST-20 and record the empty plan list rather than inventing an identifier of their own.
evidence: Legacy metadata table of RWB-E4-029 lists Epic, Module, Feature, Process, Priority, Depends on and Decision. Business Requirements Program v4 REQ-S5-008: Title transfer is prepared and recorded for vehicles and for property, Must, Sale officer, E4. TSD S5 T8 tabulates REQ-S5-001 to REQ-S5-010 against FEAT-AST-01 and FEAT-AST-08 only. Plan reqs lists of RWB-S5-E4029-APP and RWB-S5-E4029-CON are empty.
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset service owner with the business analyst of the Asset module
proposed: Trace both slices to REQ-S5-008 and FEAT-AST-20 of FSD S5 A2.20, keep the plan's empty reqs list, and let the PRD of S5 allocate the slice identifiers.

title: The FSD S5, the TSD S5 and the Epics 3 to 8 Specification that the two slices read are in review with empty sign-off tables and the realigned stories have no approval
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (document control, document sign-off); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (document control, document sign-off); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (document control); Template and Rules v1 R8.1; AGENTS.md rules 9 and 10
section: Metadata row Status of both stories; APP s3 Preconditions; CON s3 Preconditions
description: The sources of both slices are not approved. The FSD S5 is at version 3 in review with an empty sign-off table, the TSD S5 is at version 2 in review with an empty sign-off table, the Epics 3 to 8 Specification that carries the feature extract is at version 3 without approval, and this run has no human approval step, so the missing approval is recorded as an assumption, both stories carry Status Draft (realignment v1) and the work continues. No behaviour and no value of either story depends on a signature, and no status of a source document is changed.
evidence: FSD S5 document control gives Status In review and its document sign-off table has empty Name, Signature and Date cells; TSD S5 v2 document control gives Status In review and its sign-off table is empty; the Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 carries a document control block with no approval; Template and Rules v1 R8.1 asks every new document for a change-log row naming D-RCV-60 and the tool line; AGENTS.md rule 9 records a missing approval as an assumption and continues in Draft.
owner_role: Solution architect and the business owner of the Asset module
proposed: Keep both stories at Draft (realignment v1) and let the verification loop collect the signatures; nothing in the build waits on them.
